correctness.rationale: Clarkson's scalar inequality gives the necessary bound \(r^p+s^p\le1\). A disjoint normalized sequence proves every strict-interior point for any finite family. Hilbert orthogonality proves the \(p=2\) boundary. For \(p>2\), strict equality in Clarkson forces lattice disjointness, making the boundary equivalent to absence of a weak unit. The proof handles all signs, quantifiers and boundary cases and uses no finite experiment as infinite-dimensional evidence.
